idea: Fractional Head of AI for professional services firms
buyer: Managing partners at 20-200 person finance, law and design firms
pain: They know they need AI leadership and cannot justify a full-time hire
v1: Two days a month with one firm
channel: Her network across finance and architecture
verdict: The best revenue structure of any consulting shape she can sell, and only four clients are needed.

why.distribution: Warm across two professions at once - funds via her career and practices via architecture.
why.demand: Fractional executive roles are an established purchase; this specific offer is untested.
why.fmf: She has held the actual remit inside a demanding professional firm, which almost no consultant has.
why.revenue_structure: Monthly retainers that renew by default while the programme runs.
why.defensibility: Relationship and embedded knowledge make her hard to displace mid-programme.
why.leverage: Her days are the product; four clients is roughly her available capacity.
why.time_to_revenue: A warm conversation to a retainer in 1-3 months.
why.tailwind: AI adoption spend in professional services, with budget already moving.
why.ceiling: £5k/mo x 4 clients = £240k, and four retainers is genuinely reachable.

ceiling_arithmetic: £5k/mo x 4 concurrent retainers = £240k/yr, negligible direct cost. Four clients at two days each is 8 days a month - demanding but feasible. Ramping in over the year: 2-3 clients = £120-180k realistic.
carries: Only four customers needed to clear the target, recurring monthly revenue, and the rarest thing she owns as the product.
kills: Leverage is 2 - this trades her calendar for money, with no asset accumulating underneath it.
test: Offer a three-month fractional arrangement at £4k/mo to two firms in her network.
test_fail: They want a project, not a person - which points at idea i006 instead.
